plan: My private value is $30. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable. If I bid more, I might pay more than the item is worth to me. Since this is a single round with no repeated interactions, bidding exactly $30 maximizes my expected profit by ensuring I win only when the item is truly worth more than the second-highest bid.

My private value is $35. To maximize profit, I want to win the auction while paying as little as possible. Since values are drawn randomly and independently, I'll aim to bid slightly above the expected average bid (around $24.50) but below my full value. A bid around $32-$33 gives me a good chance of winning while preserving potential profit margin. This strategy balances winning probability with maintaining earnings if I win.

My private value is $6, which means I want to win only if the item costs less than $6. My optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit. Since values are randomly drawn, I'll bid $5.9 - this gives me a chance to win if others bid lower, and ensures I don't overpay. This strategy protects my potential profit margin while still being competitive.
